criteria.text: The participant has histologically or cytologically documented non-squamous NSCLC.
The participant has Stage III B/C or IV NSCLC (based on the American Joint Committee on Cancer Edition 8) not amenable to curative treatment.

The participant does not have sensitizing EGFR mutations (including, but not limited to, exon 19 deletion and exon 21 L858R, exon 21 L861Q, exon 18 G719X, and exon 20 S768I mutations) and ALK and ROS1 rearrangements.

The participant does not have documented tumor genomic mutation results from tests conducted as part of standard local practice in any other actionable driver oncogenes for which there are locally approved and available targeted 1L therapies.
The participant provides an acceptable tumor sample to confirm tumor PD-L1 expression TC ≥ 1%.

The participant has at least one lesion not previously irradiated that qualifies as a RECIST 1.1 TL at baseline and can be accurately measured at baseline as ≥ 10 mm in the longest diameter (except lymph nodes, which must have short axis ≥ 15 mm) with CT or MRI and is suitable for accurate repeated measurements.
The participant has adequate organ and bone marrow function.
The participant has small cell and neuroendocrine histology components.

The participant has brain metastases unless asymptomatic, stable, and not requiring steroids or anticonvulsants for at least 7 days prior to randomization. A minimum of 2 weeks must have elapsed between the end of local therapy (brain radiotherapy or surgery) and randomization. Participants must have recovered from the acute toxic effect of radiotherapy (eg, dizziness and signs of increased intracranial pressure) or surgery prior to randomization.

The participant has any prior systemic therapy received for NSCLC except in the neoadjuvant or adjuvant setting or definitive chemoradiotherapy with the intent to cure, provided that progression has occurred > 12 months after the end of systemic therapy treatment.
The participant has any prior exposure to an anti-TIGIT therapy or any other anticancer therapy targeting immune-regulatory receptors or mechanisms.
The participant has any prior treatment with an anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 agent.

The participant has a history of another primary malignancy except for malignancy treated with curative intent with no known active disease ≥ 2 years before the first dose of study intervention and of low potential risk for recurrence.

The participant has active or prior documented autoimmune or inflammatory disorders requiring chronic systemic treatment with the use of disease-modifying agents, corticosteroids, or immunosuppressive drugs.
The participant has active primary immunodeficiency/active infectious disease(s).
The participant has active tuberculosis infection.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Global Phase III Study of Rilvegostomig or Pembrolizumab Plus Chemotherapy for First-Line Treatment of Locally Advanced or Metastatic Non-Squamous NSCLC". Your earlier answers already covered 4 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever been tested for EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 genetic changes in your tumor? These are specific mutations that can affect treatment options. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't remember, dear. I'm not sure, you'd have to ask my neighbor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had any other genetic tests on your tumor for different mutations, besides EGFR, ALK, or ROS1, that were part of your regular care?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Oh, I don't know. I'm not sure, you'd have to ask my neighbor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had your tumor tissue tested for PD-L1 expression? This is a protein level measured on tumor cells to help guide treatment. If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't remember, dear. I'm not sure, you'd have to ask my neighbor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had a recent CT or MRI scan showing a tumor spot that hasn't been treated with radiation yet, and is at least 10 mm wide (or 15 mm for lymph nodes)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure, you'd have to ask my neighbor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you had recent blood tests to check that your liver, kidneys, and bone marrow are working well enough for treatment? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know, dear. I'm not sure, you'd have to ask my neighbor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you know if your cancer diagnosis includes small cell or neuroendocrine types? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't remember, dear. I know it's non-small cell, but I don't recall the specific cell type.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever received chemotherapy, immunotherapy, or targeted therapy for your lung cancer before this study? This includes treatment given before or after surgery if the goal was to cure the cancer.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I had the carboplatin with my radiation. But I haven't had the immune one or the pill aimed at the mutation.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever received any treatment specifically targeting TIGIT or other immune-regulatory receptors? If you aren't sure, that's okay.

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know, dear. I'm not sure, you'd have to ask my neighbor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with a different type of cancer, other than your current lung cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I had something taken off my skin once, I think it was a cancer, but I don't remember what kind or when.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: The trial asks about this: “The participant has a history of another primary malignancy except for malignancy treated with curative intent with no known active disease ≥ 2 years before the first dose of study intervention and of low potential risk for recurrence.”. Does this describe you?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't remember, dear. I had something taken off my skin once, but I don't know if it was cured or how long ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you currently have an autoimmune or inflammatory condition (like rheumatoid arthritis or lupus) that requires daily medication such as steroids or immune-suppressing drugs?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have that kind of condition.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you currently have an active infection, such as pneumonia or a urinary tract infection, or a condition that weakens your immune system (like HIV)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have HIV. I don't know about any active infections like pneumonia right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have a known condition where your immune system doesn't work properly from birth (primary immunodeficiency)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't know, dear. I'm not sure, you'd have to ask my neighbor.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with active tuberculosis (TB)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have tuberculosis.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
